title: Grammar: Advanced Learner Mistakes
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan explains the most common grammar mistakes made by advanced English learners — misuse of articles, prepositions, and complex tenses — and how to fix them.

title: Grammar: Present to Talk About the Past
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan explores the 'historical present' — how English speakers use present tenses to tell past stories, narrate sports, and create dramatic effects.

title: Grammar: Formal English and Informal English
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan breaks down the key differences between formal and informal English — vocabulary choices, grammatical structures, and when to use each register.

title: Grammar: Giving Emphasis in English
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan teaches advanced emphasis structures — cleft sentences, fronting, and do-support — to make English more expressive and persuasive.

title: Grammar: 'Mistakes' Native English Speakers Make
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan reveals common grammatical 'mistakes' that native English speakers make — and explains which ones are now considered acceptable in modern usage.

title: Grammar: Mixing Conditionals
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan teaches mixed conditionals — combining different conditional forms to talk about unreal situations with complex time relationships between past and present.

title: Grammar: Question Tags
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan explains how to form and use question tags in British English — including the difference between falling and rising intonation and how tags function in natural conversation.

title: Grammar: Linking Words of Contrast
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan presents four key ways to express contrast in English — although, despite, however, and while — with clear examples of when and how to use each.

title: Grammar: More Advanced Learner Mistakes
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan continues the advanced learner mistakes series — covering more subtle errors in grammar and usage that prevent advanced speakers from sounding fully natural.

title: Grammar: Using 'What' to Give Emphasis
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan dives into 'what' as a focus marker in cleft sentences — a powerful structure that adds emphasis and contrast, often misused by even advanced learners.

title: Useful Phrases for English Conversation
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan shares a collection of the most useful phrases for natural English conversation — from agreeing and disagreeing to hedging, softening, and changing the subject.

title: Inversion 1: After Negative or Limiting Adverbs
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan introduces inversion after negative adverbs like 'never', 'rarely', and 'not only' — a formal structure used for emphasis in written and spoken English.

title: Inversion 2: Reduced Conditionals and More
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan covers reduced conditionals ('Had I known...', 'Were I to...') and other advanced inversions — formal structures found in literary, academic, and professional English.

title: How to Choose the Correct Tense in English
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan tackles one of the most confusing areas for English learners — when to use the present perfect vs. past simple, and other key tense distinctions in context.

title: How to Use Linking Words in English
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan explains how to use discourse markers and linking words to structure arguments, add information, show cause and effect, and improve coherence in writing and speaking.

title: Grammar: 'Stop Buying' or 'Stop to Buy'?
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Dan explains the difference between gerunds and infinitives after verbs like 'stop', 'remember', 'try', and 'regret' — verbs that change meaning depending on which form follows.
